title: Blinded development-image review, followed by label/prediction comparison

provenance.images: Only approved development copies case_01.jpg through case_30.jpg and blind_sheet_01.jpg through blind_sheet_05.jpg were viewed. Tick IDs resolve original source paths and source hashes through the hashed train/dev manifest.
provenance.review_method: Two parallel reviewers recorded morphology before accessing mapping, labels, predictions, or error status. Reviewer A inspected all contact sheets and selected original details; reviewer B inspected all 30 originals. This report joins their frozen reports after completion.
provenance.verification: Independent read-only verification confirmed all mapping labels, predictions, stages, and probability vectors; exactly all 15 first-round errors plus 15 correct development controls; all 110 validation IDs match the manifest development IDs; manifest hash matches model provenance.

interpretation.observations_are_not_replacement_labels: Limited/intermediate/marked describe apparent projected morphology. They do not equal Penn unengorged/semi-engorged/fully engorged classes and are not verified replacement labels. No labels changed.
interpretation.clarity: Reviewer A clear/ambiguous refers to visibility of the stated structural observation, not certainty of a biological grade. Reviewer B broad confidence is distinct from exact grade confidence.
interpretation.resize: Reviewer A resize risk is a qualitative expectation for full-frame resizing to 320 or 384 pixels; no actual resized-image experiment was performed. The evaluated model uses 384-pixel letterbox with 4% bottom crop, so these flags are hypotheses rather than measured preprocessing failures.
interpretation.exact_grading: Reviewer B certified no exact flat/slight/intermediate/full grade from these single photographs. This conservative statement is not evidence that every image is unusable.
interpretation.disagreements: Both observations remain recorded; no retrospective consensus class or relabeling was imposed after unblinding.

reviewer_agreement.meaning: The 11 disagreements include visibly folded bodies with readable proportions as well as damaged specimens. They show rubric/boundary uncertainty, not evidence that original labels are wrong.

findings: Ambiguous evidence was common in both selected groups (A: 9/15 errors, 8/15 controls). Oblique views also occurred in both (3/15 errors, 4/15 controls). Both ventral cases (23 and 28) were errors, but two selected observations do not establish an association or causal explanation.
High qualitative resize risk was more common among controls (10/15) than errors (5/15). Small occupancy and potential detail loss therefore do not explain the observed errors by themselves.

Bodies with damage, folds, or irregular margins occur among errors (07, 11, 12, 20) and correct controls (06). Large projected area does not reliably reveal intact volume. Ventral cases 23 and 28 lack an exposed dorsal shield in both reviews.

Some model-label disagreements remain despite readable anatomy: cases 03 and 22 have clear structural evidence under reviewer A, while reviewers disagree on limited versus intermediate morphology. Cases 18 and 20 both appear markedly expanded to both reviewers but carry semi-engorged labels; case 20 is damaged. These are unresolved boundaries, not confirmed annotation errors.

The smallest training joint groups are adult female semi-engorged (7 train, 5 dev; 4/5 first-round errors) and nymph fully engorged (9 train, 7 dev; 2/7 errors). Nymph unengorged has only 5 dev cases (21 train; 3/5 errors). These sparse supports warrant retaining subgroup counts beside aggregate metrics.

The dominant nymph semi-engorged group has 155 train and 63 dev cases, with 5/63 errors. Adult female fully engorged has 13 train and 9 dev, with 0/9 errors. Small-group success or failure is unstable, and the chosen model was selected using this development set.
decisions_and_testable_implications: Retain all original labels and all development cases in evaluation. Preserve disagreement and damaged-view uncertainty explicitly.

Assess the queued crop and auxiliary-stage experiments against unchanged development predictions and the rare joint subgroups; this review alone does not justify adopting a new preprocessing rule or model.

A future anatomy-focused crop should retain the entire shield and abdominal outline, preserve aspect ratio, and be audited on damaged, ventral, low-occupancy, and glare-heavy images. Higher resolution cannot recover hidden anatomy or saturated detail.

Keep view, shield visibility, quality, and specimen-integrity flags separate from the biological target. If abstention is later evaluated, report coverage and performance over the full development set without silently excluding cases.

Use uncertainty-aware outputs for adjacent-class boundaries and investigate stage-conditioned errors without turning stage or background into a deterministic class shortcut. No code or label changes are made by this review.
limitations: This is a deliberately error-enriched audit: all 15 errors from 110 development cases plus 15 of 95 correct cases. Its 50% error fraction and visual flag proportions are not prevalence estimates.

Protocol describes controls as matched_or_random_correct_controls but does not provide matching rules or sampling probabilities. No matched analysis, significance claim, or causal association is justified.

Reviewers share the supplied photographs and broad instructions; their agreement is not an independent biological reference. Reviewer A inspected selected originals while reviewer B inspected all originals.
Single views, deformation, unknown intact thickness, glare, and unclear boundaries limit interpretation. Color, apparent size, and damage cannot verify engorgement, feeding time, or disease risk.
The model and audit were chosen on development data; repeated development analysis can overfit decisions. No test images were viewed or used.
Rare joint subgroup denominators are small. The descriptive first-round errors are not new held-out performance estimates, and no reviewed case was removed from development metrics.

followup_training_review.selection: All seven training adult female semi-engorged images plus seven unengorged adult female training controls, seed20261019. Label-aware, exploratory.
followup_training_review.findings: All seven rare examples expose dorsal anatomy with a readable scutum/body relation. Some show distinguishable posterior/lateral extent; 286815 overlaps control289909 in gross shape; irregular outlines/glare occur in others. Repetition can increase useful exposure and also repeat ambiguity/artifacts.
followup_training_review.root_confirmation: Inspected original training photos286815 and289909; broad elongated shape and prominent scutum overlap. No replacement grade assigned.
